help.title: About Product orders
help.overview: A product order is one customer purchase from the shop, or one till sale mirrored for the books. Checkout writes it; this page never creates one. Each order carries three statuses that move separately — the order, the payment, and the fulfillment — plus a timeline of every step and who took it.

sections.title: How an order is created
sections.body: The order is the end of checkout, not the start.
items: Checkout first re-prices the cart from the live catalog, then holds stock for every tracked line before any money is taken. If a line cannot be covered, checkout stops and nothing is held.
Card payments create the order when the payment succeeds, either on the buyer's confirmation or from the payment webhook, whichever arrives first. The order is written only once.
Cash on delivery and bank transfer create a pending, unpaid order. Staff confirm it and mark it paid when the money arrives.
A checkout that is never completed expires after its time limit; a job releases its held stock every hour. If its payment did go through, the job places the order instead.
On the platform shop, a cart with several sellers becomes one order per seller company.

sections.title: The three statuses
sections.body: Read them together. An order can be paid and still unfulfilled, or shipped and partly refunded.
items: Order status: pending, confirmed, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded.
Payment status: unpaid, authorized, paid, partially refunded, refunded, voided.
Fulfillment status: unfulfilled, partially fulfilled, fulfilled, returned. It is derived from the order's shipments.
Shipped and delivered are also derived: shipped once every line has left, delivered once every shipment that did not fail is delivered.

sections.title: Row actions
sections.body: Each action is refused outside the state it expects. Status actions need permission to write the order status; money actions need permission to write the payment status.
items: Confirm is only from pending. It acknowledges the order and tells the customer.
Mark processing is only from confirmed. It means the order is being prepared.

Ship is from confirmed or processing. It creates one shipment for every quantity still unshipped, takes those units out of stock, and records the carrier, tracking number, and tracking link the customer is sent.

Mark paid records an offline payment with an optional reference, only while the payment is unpaid and the order is not cancelled or refunded. A pending order is confirmed at the same time, and gift cards and downloads bought with the order are issued.

Cancel is blocked once the order is shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded, and a paid order must be refunded first. It releases the stock still held and gives back store credit paid with a gift card.
Refund is for a paid or partially refunded order, in full or by an amount. A card payment is refunded through the gateway; an offline payment is recorded as a manual refund.

sections.title: What a full refund undoes
sections.body: A partial refund only moves money. A refund of everything that is left also unwinds what the order gave out.
items: Store credit spent on the order goes back to the gift card.
Gift cards the order issued are disabled, and its download links expire.
Stock still held for unshipped lines is released. Units that already shipped come back only through a received return request.
The order becomes refunded. A till sale cannot be refunded here: it is refunded on the till, which keeps the drawer and the stock in step.

sections.title: Customer messages and the timeline
sections.body: The buyer is told at each step that matters to them, after the change is saved.
items: Confirmation, shipping (with tracking), delivery, payment, cancellation, refund, and return decisions each send the customer a notification and email.
Every action adds a timeline entry with the time, the staff member, and any note, reference, or tracking number.
Notes are visible to the customer; internal notes are for staff only.

sections.title: Where the rest of the work is
sections.body: The order is the header. Shipments and returns are their own records.
items: Each shipment is a row under Fulfillments, with its own pending, shipped, delivered, or failed status.
A return, exchange, or refund request is a row under Return requests. Completing one can refund this order.
Till sales appear here as already delivered and paid, marked as POS sales, with an in-store pickup address.
Deleting an order is a soft delete and it can be restored.
